observations: Frame and gap losses have finite correctly directed target/background readout derivatives and nonzero gradients in original TPro, conv_out1 and conv_out2 in all8 actual GPU training batches.
Old feature contrast alone has zero direct conv_out2 gradient; this is the known graph topology, not proof it cannot indirectly affect logits.
Most target ROI-mean logits remain below zero in the segment exposure pool; ROI means are a training proxy, not actual-component matches.
Selected current-model background logits are already very negative, so readout gradients mainly raise target evidence at calibration; the background branch is present but usually much weaker.

Both additions align with detection gradients and oppose keep gradients on all8 batches. They oppose the total C-v1 gradient in3 batches, so preserving previous responses remains a measured optimization tradeoff.
limitations: Contrast statistics use the unchanged v1 pair subset; risk readouts use the expanded segment pool. Comparing their aggregate values does not identify a causal feature/readout mismatch on identical observations.
Calibration proves numerical/graph connection only, with no parameter update and no development result inspected.
One easy frame may satisfy gap; order within a segment is invariant; neither property guarantees sustained detection recovery.
